But the period on which we now enter did more than merely coincide with the end of one century and the beginning of another.

73184-four-years-in-upper-burma.description: A book by W. R. Winston.. much closer touch with England; and many people, by no means ignorant of Burma before, now feel a much deeper interest than formerly in all that pertains to that interesting country, whose destinies are henceforth so intimately bound up with our own.

arxiv-2203-03468.title: Loss of material trainability through an unusual transition
arxiv-2203-03468.creator: Himangsu Bhaumik, Daniel Hexner
arxiv-2203-03468.description: Abstract Material training is a method to endow materials with specific responses through external driving. We study the complexity of attainable responses, as expressed in the number of sites that are simultaneously controlled. With increased complexity, convergence to the desired response becomes very slow.

arxiv-2207-10576.title: Democratizing Ethical Assessment of Natural Language Generation Models DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: Make sure to enter the correct conference title from your rights confirmation email; August 14–18, 2022; Washington, DC KDD ’22: SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining, August 14
arxiv-2207-10576.creator: Amin Rasekh, Ian Eisenberg
arxiv-2207-10576.description: Abstract . Natural language generation models are computer systems that generate coherent language when prompted with a sequence of words as context. Despite their ubiquity and many beneficial applications, language generation models also have the potential to inflict social harms by generating discriminatory language, hateful speech, profane content, and other harmful material. Ethical assessment of these models is therefore critical.

arxiv-2311-08021.title: Silhouettes and generic properties of subgroups of the modular group Thanks: LaBRI, Univ. Bordeaux, 351 cours de la Libération, 33400 Talence, France.
arxiv-2311-08021.creator: Frédérique Bassino, bassino@lipn.fr, Cyril Nicaud, cyril.nicaud@u-pem.fr, Pascal Weil, pascal.weil@labri.fr
arxiv-2311-08021.description: Abstract We show that the probability for a finitely generated subgroup of the modular group, of size n n , to be almost malnormal or non-parabolic, tends to 0 as n n tends to infinity — where the notion of the size of a subgroup is based on a natural graph-theoretic representation of the subgroup.

arxiv-2312-00563.title: Investigations in Calabi-Yau Modularity and Mirror Symmetry
arxiv-2312-00563.creator: Joseph McGovern
arxiv-2312-00563.description: Abstract This thesis lays out a number of different projects, linked by the common thread of Calabi-Yau manifolds. We produce tables of instanton numbers for various multiparameter Calabi-Yau manifolds. Studying those tables reveals, in some cases, a Coxeter group of symmetries that act on sets of instanton numbers.

arxiv-2404-09643.title: The first detection of X-ray polarization in a newly discovered Galactic transient Swift J151857.0-572147
arxiv-2404-09643.creator: Santanu Mondal, S. Pujitha Suribhatla, Kaushik Chatterjee, Chandra B. Singh, Rwitika Chatterjee
arxiv-2404-09643.description: Abstract We study the spectro-polarimetric properties of a newly discovered black hole X-ray binary Swift J151857.0-572147 jointly using IXPE and NuSTAR observations during March 2024. The analysis of IXPE data reports the first detection of X-ray polarization with degree (PD) 1.34 ± 0.27 1.34\pm 0.27 and polarization angle (PA) − 13.69 ∘ ± 5.85 ∘ -13.69^{\circ}\pm 5.

arxiv-2507-11598.title: Why Did the Dark Matter Hypothesis Supersede Modified Gravity in the 1980s? Thanks: This article appears in Studies in History and Philosophy of Science , 112, pp.141-152. For citing purposes please refer to the published version at: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.shpsa.2025.06.006
arxiv-2507-11598.creator: Antonis Antoniou
arxiv-2507-11598.description: Abstract . In the 1960s and 1970s a series of observations and theoretical developments highlighted the presence of several anomalies which could, in principle, be explained by postulating one of the following two working hypotheses: (i) the existence of dark matter, or (ii) the modification of standard gravitational dynamics in low accelerations.

arxiv-2509-16157.title: Strategic Analysis of Just-In-Time Liquidity Provision in Concentrated Liquidity Market Makers
arxiv-2509-16157.creator: Bruno Llacer Trotti, Weizhao Tang, Rachid El-Azouzi, Giulia Fanti, Daniel Sadoc Menasché
arxiv-2509-16157.description: Abstract Liquidity providers (LPs) are essential figures in the operation of automated market makers (AMMs); in exchange for transaction fees, LPs lend the liquidity that allows AMMs to operate. While many prior works have studied the incentive structures of LPs in general, we currently lack a principled understanding of a special class of LPs known as Just-In-Time (JIT) LPs.

arxiv-2510-17350.title: Sobolev instability for perturbations of periodic transport equations
arxiv-2510-17350.creator: Gabriel Rivière, Maria Teresa Rotolo
arxiv-2510-17350.description: Abstract We consider linear and time-dependent perturbations of periodic transport equations on the two-dimensional torus. For generic perturbations, we prove the existence of a large class of initial data whose Sobolev norms diverge exponentially fast. In higher dimensions, this remains true under a Morse-Smale assumption on the resonant part of the perturbation.

pmc-10534554.title: Population-Based Screening for Coeliac Disease in Lithuanian Children from 2009 to 2014
pmc-10534554.creator: Vaidotas Urbonas, Jolita Sadauskaite, Dominykas Varnas, Renata Talar-Wojnarowska
pmc-10534554.description: Background and Objectives. Coeliac disease is an autoimmune disorder provoked by a dietary group of proteins called gluten in genetically predisposed individuals. Over the past several decades, the prevalence of coeliac disease has been steadily growing and it is now recognized to be occurring worldwide. The prevalence varies greatly between ethnic, racial groups and regionally.

pmc-10556626.title: A predatory gastrula leads to symbiosis-independent settlement in Aiptasia
pmc-10556626.creator: Ira Maegele, Sebastian Rupp, Suat Özbek, Annika Guse, Elizabeth A. Hambleton, Thomas W. Holstein
pmc-10556626.description: The planula larvae of the sea anemone Aiptasia have so far not been reported to complete their life cycle by undergoing metamorphosis into adult forms. This has been a major obstacle in their use as a model for coral–dinoflagellate endosymbiosis. Here, we show that Aiptasia larvae actively feed on crustacean nauplii, displaying a preference for live prey.

pmc-11436697.title: High-throughput dataset of impurity adsorption on common catalysts in biomass upgrading applications
pmc-11436697.creator: Michelle A. Nolen, Sean A. Tacey, Martha A. Arellano-Treviño, Kurt M. Van Allsburg, Carrie A. Farberow
pmc-11436697.description: An extensive dataset consisting of adsorption energies of pernicious impurities present in biomass upgrading processes on common catalysts and support materials has been generated. This work aims to inform catalyst and process development for the conversion of biomass-derived feedstocks to fuels and chemicals.

pmc-11465213.title: Management strategies for neglected simultaneous bilateral femoral neck fractures: Case report and literature review
pmc-11465213.creator: Arvin Najafi, Salman Azarsina, Dorsa Hadavi, Rahele Arkian, Sevak Hatamian, Pouria Chaghamirzayi
pmc-11465213.description: Introduction and importanceSimultaneous bilateral femoral neck fractures are rare and challenging, often occurring due to high-energy trauma in younger adults or low-energy trauma compounded by metabolic issues in elderly populations. Neglected cases, particularly in the context of narcotic addiction and limited access to healthcare, present unique management dilemmas.

pmc-11579512.title: Deoxybouvardin-glucoside induces apoptosis in non-small cell lung cancer cells by targeting EGFR/MET and AKT signaling pathway
pmc-11579512.creator: Na Yeong Lee, Sang Hoon Joo, A-Young Nam, Seung-On Lee, Goo Yoon, Seung-Sik Cho, Yung Hyun Choi, Jin Woo Park, Jung-Hyun Shim
pmc-11579512.description: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is a leading cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide. Its treatment is complicated due to the development of resistance to conventional chemotherapy and targeted therapy. Deoxybouvardin and related cyclic hexapeptides reportedly exhibit antitumor activities, but their mechanisms of action remain unclear.

pmc-11624696.title: Potential research priorities for understanding and treating severe paranoia (persecutory delusions): a priority-setting partnership between patients, carers, mental health staff, and researchers
pmc-11624696.creator: David Ariel Sher, Thomas Kabir, Maurice Arbuthnott, Suzie Nettleton, Pauline Dixon, Joanna May, Alvaro Barrera, Poppy Brown, Sarah Reeve, Louise Isham, Felicity Waite, Daniel Freeman
pmc-11624696.description: BackgroundA persecutory delusion (severe paranoia) occurs when a person believes that others are trying to harm them when they are not. It is often a central difficulty for patients diagnosed with schizophrenia.ObjectiveThe objective is to identify potentially important research questions about severe paranoia.MethodsA priority-setting partnership exercise was conducted involving people with lived experience, carers, mental health staff, and researchers.

pmc-12413844.title: Associations Between Inflammatory and Catecholamine Markers and Clinical Outcomes in People with Post-Acute SARS-CoV-2 Infection
pmc-12413844.creator: Lynn H Gerber, Micahel Estep, Leyla De Avila, Jillian K Price, Ali A Weinstein, Maria Stepanova, Aybike Birerdinc, Zobair Younossi
pmc-12413844.description: PurposeThe diagnosis of post-acute SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC) is broad, referring to new or persistent health problems >four weeks after being infected with SARSCoV-2. The aim of this study was to determine whether cytokines, chemokines or catecholamine levels could specify the clinical condition.Patients and MethodsSeventy-nine participants participated in person to study PASC.

pmc-12607739.title: Arterial Enhancement Fraction-Spectral CT-Based Model as Part of Prediction Model in BRAFV600E-Positive Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma
pmc-12607739.creator: Bi Zhou, Liang Lv, Ya Zou, Zuhua Song, Jiayi Yu, Xiaodi Zhang, Dan Zhang, Mara Carsote
pmc-12607739.description: Objectives: The BRAFV600E is the most common oncogene in thyroid cancer and is associated with the aggressiveness of papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC). The aim of this study was to investigate the effectiveness of the arterial enhancement fraction (AEF) and dual-layer detector spectral computed tomography (DLCT) parameters for predicting the BRAFV600E mutation in PTC.

pmc-12780456.title: Thoracic morphological characteristics of primary spontaneous pneumothorax patients requiring surgical intervention
pmc-12780456.creator: Ryo Nonomura, Hiromichi Niikawa, Ryuga Yabe, Hideyuki Nagata, Kazunori Ueda, Yutaka Oshima, Takanobu Sasaki, Naoya Ishibashi, Hirohito Metoki
pmc-12780456.description: BackgroundPrimary spontaneous pneumothorax (PSP) is a condition commonly observed in adolescents, often associated with physical characteristics such as tall stature, low body weight, and a flat thoracic cage. However, the relationship between thoracic morphology and the development of PSP remains unclear.

pmc-13197110.title: Pulse Discovery Toolkit, a Multicomponent Nutrition Intervention for Preschool Children in Childcare Centers: Mixed Methods Pilot Study
pmc-13197110.creator: Hiwot Abebe Haileslassie, Renee Ramikie, Hassan Vatanparast, D Dan Ramdath, Amanda Froehlich Chow, Phyllis Shand, Rachel Engler-Stringer, Jessica R L Lieffers, Shannon Hood-Niefer, Carol Henry, Matthew Balcarras
pmc-13197110.description: BackgroundChildren’s eating habits are formed at an early age, making childhood a crucial period for introducing novel foods, such as pulse-based food products. Pulse Discovery Toolkit (PDTK) intervention was designed to increase familiarity with pulses and to eventually contribute to the consumption of pulse-based foods among preschool children in childcare centers (CCs).

pmc-13605831.title: Radiation-Induced Morphea of the Breast in a Patient with Pre-Existing Mycosis Fungoides: A Diagnostic Challenge
pmc-13605831.creator: Tala Mobayed, Toufic Eid, Ossama Abbas, Hiba Moukadem, Nagi El Saghir, Zeina Ayoub
pmc-13605831.description: Simple SummaryRadiotherapy for breast cancer can rarely cause radiation-induced morphea, in which the skin becomes thickened and hardened months to years after treatment. Diagnosis can be challenging, particularly in patients with a history of mycosis fungoides, because both conditions may appear similar.
